title: OKR Harmonization Runway and Initiative Prioritization Rubric
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
We need a repeatable, transparent rubric and a time-phased runway to harmonize company-level OKRs with engineering and GTM initiatives so that leadership can make trade-off decisions across Dedicated, Private, and Hosted product areas. This ticket delivers: (1) a prioritization rubric (quantitative + qualitative) for scoring initiatives against OKRs, (2) a runway mapping showing initiative start/finish windows and gating decisions, and (3) a handoff playbook for cross-functional owners to escalate scope or resource conflicts during quarterly cycles.

Background:
During the last planning cycle (2025-Q4 -> 2026-Q1) several initiative collisions occurred: two teams requested Dedicated capacity increases for the same quarter, and the Console rollout and Optimize cost experiment clashed on shared platform capacity. Leadership requested a clearer way to score initiatives against company-level OKRs and a visible runway with decision gates to prevent last-minute re-scopes.

Goals (success criteria):
- Provide a rubric that yields a defensible numeric score for each initiative and maps to a recommended priority band (A/B/C).
- Publish a runway Gantt for 3 quarters with explicit gating dates and SLA-like escalation paths.
- Run rubric calibration workshops with Eng, Product, Design, Sales, and Customer Success; achieve >=80% alignment on top-10 initiatives.
- Reduce mid-cycle scope swaps involving Dedicated capacity by 50% (tracked via change log).

Proposed Prioritization Rubric (draft weights):
- OKR alignment (company-level impact): 35%
- Customer urgency / revenue risk (real dollar impact): 20%
- Operational risk / reliability improvement (SLO uplift): 15%
- Cost reduction / unit economics (per-token savings estimate): 10%
- Implementation effort (story points & infra ops): -10% (penalty)
- Cross-org dependency complexity: -5% (penalty)
- Strategic runway / platform fit (long-term platform thesis): 15%
Scoring notes: each axis scored 0-10, final weighted score 0-10. Bands: 8.0+ (A), 5.0-7.9 (B), <5.0 (C).

Runway & Decision Gates (draft):
- T-16w: Intake scoring window opens; RMs submit initiative PRD link and provisional estimate.
- T-12w: Cross-functional review (rubric calibration session).
- T-8w: Resource commitment confirmed (eng + infra budgets).
- T-4w: Final scope freeze; any changes require Exec approval and change log update.
- Post-launch +4w: Retro and quality signal evaluation mapped to OKR metrics.

Trade-offs considered:
- Quantity vs. depth: scoring allows many small experiments but will favor high-scoring strategic bets — we propose reserving a 15% experimentation bucket each quarter.
- Precision of cost estimates: per-token and Dedicated capacity cost models are noisy; we use 90th percentile conservative estimates and require cost owners to sign off.
- Speed vs. reliability: gating enforces freezes that may delay fast-follow features; we recommend a fast-track exception flow for urgent security/compliance fixes.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: rubric gamification by teams inflating scores. Mitigation: cross-org calibration meetings and requirement to attach evidence (customer quotes, telemetry dashboards, revenue impact calc).
- Risk: inaccurate effort estimates causing wrong prioritization. Mitigation: require engineering leads to supply three-point estimates and flag variance >30% pre-launch.

- Rubric spreadsheet (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/okrs/rubric-v0.3 (has scoring template + sample scoring for 12 initiatives)
- Runway Gantt (Figma/Sheets): https://sheets.redwood.ai/okrs/runway-2026-q1-3
- Sample dashboard (Looker): https://looker.redwood.ai/dashboards/okrs-alignment
- Example GH issue for Dedicated capacity dispute: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/42812

Stakeholder engagement plan:
- Week of 2026-02-16: Calibration workshop with Eng leads (runtime, infra, console) and Sales AE leads (M&E customers).
- Week of 2026-02-23: Draft rubric published to exec; 48h comment window.
- 2026-03-05: Leadership review (scheduled) to validate weighting and approve runway gates.

Progress updates (timeline of ticket activity):
- 2026-02-10 (Maya Chen): Created ticket and uploaded v0.1 rubric to Drive. Requested initial scoring examples from Eng and CS.
- 2026-02-17 (Aisha Raman): Ran calibration session with Eng runtime and infra; revised weighting to increase OKR alignment weight from 30% -> 35% after runtime impact examples. Notes attached in rubric spreadsheet.
- 2026-02-24 (Aisha Raman): Received sample scoring from Sales for top-5 paying customers; adjusted revenue impact scoring guidance.
- 2026-03-01 (Maya Chen): Updated PRD v0.3 with gating language and exception flow. Added change-log template for mid-cycle scope changes.
- 2026-03-05 (Aisha Raman): Leadership review completed. Execs requested an explicit experiment quota (15%) and a fast-track security exception process. Action: incorporate into v0.4 and distribute for final sign-off.

Open decisions and asks for reviewers:
- Confirm final weightings and whether to treat platform-level SLO improvements as multiplicative to OKR alignment (proposal: multiply OKR alignment score by 1.1 if initiative improves SLO >10%).
- Approve the 15% experimentation reserve or propose alternative guardrail.
- Confirm the Exec approval path for fast-track exceptions (who signs off, SLA for decision).

Next steps (owner assignments):
- Aisha: incorporate leadership feedback and publish rubric v0.4 by 2026-03-12. (In flight)
- Eng leads (runtime, infra): provide three-point effort estimates for top-10 scored initiatives by 2026-03-18.
- CS/Sales: attach customer impact evidence for initiatives touching top-20 accounts by 2026-03-18.
- PMs: run the scoring template on current backlog and present prioritized list in the 2026-Q2 planning offsite (2026-03-25).

Approval log:
- 2026-03-05: Exec align (CTO Jonah Patel, CRO Elena Voss) — feedback captured; final approval pending after v0.4 updates.

Comments (recent):
- 2026-03-02 (Jonah Patel): "We need a clear escalation SLA for capacity conflicts — suggest 24h Exec decision for production-impacting conflicts."
- 2026-03-03 (Elena Voss): "Agree on experiment bucket. Also ask finance to validate revenue impact calc for FY26 estimates."
- 2026-03-04 (SRE lead Luis Martinez): "Suggest adding a reliability multiplier so that high-SLO uplift projects get prioritized for infra windows."

Acceptance criteria for this ticket (ready to close):
- Rubric v0.4 published in Confluence and Drive with sample scoring applied to 12 active initiatives.
- Runway Gantt published and integrated into Planning playbook.
- Exec sign-off recorded in approval log (signature by CTO or COO).
- Calibration session notes attached and >80% of cross-functional attendees mark alignment as "agree" in the post-session survey.

If you are a stakeholder, please review the PRD and rubric spreadsheet and add evidence for initiatives you own. For questions or to join calibration sessions, ping #okrs-runway in Slack.
